title: Working line: the bot's mark and what it is doing now
evidence: Working line in Transcript.tsx + styles.css: row 180 ms, mark 340 ms spring, label 180 ms (+220 ms first), shimmer steps(60) 2.2 s, face squash and tilt, exit 140 ms. Starts with the mark alone, like the oracle; "Typing…" while text streams (not for text that lands within a frame). Gate B: "replied" lands with the reply bubble (0.79.3: the same ms on all 4 turns; ours 2–3 ms after, was ~103 ms, which put it after storage's Unread dot) and the exit is inside budget on 4 turns, long-answer (Grok 0.79.3) included: one reply of 1214 characters after 4.2 s of "Typing…", line gone 240 ms after it. The row comes with the bot's Working state (Barkpark's fleet stream, event: state), as the oracle's comes with its rail's Working: storage's row 0.8 s after "is working" now matches (Gate B working#1, 2016 vs 2014 ms; a row ignoring the state fails it, early by 776 ms). The rail's Working was judged as its own Gate B moment on the three 0.79.2 traces (rail:working, within 3 ms; from the turn's start it failed storage, early by 777 ms); those are superseded by the 0.79.3 re-records of 2026-11-10, which show no Working on the open bot. 0.79.3 never says Working on the open bot (long-answer), so there the line is the state's only witness: the stand-in flips it at the line (turn.ts, fromRow); the UI holding the line 300 ms longer fails working#1, late by 303 ms. Tool labels: a host with item events (task-f13fc4b4dc2af6de) sends each tool call with its name and input, and the line says it (Bash's description, else the tool). The bot's own summary of the turn ("Mulling it over", "Checking the storage", "Explaining ocean tides"): Barkpark #26296 sends it as event: runtime {kind: status, native: {label}}, once a turn before the first text; the line says it as plain words (60 at most), and one that comes after the text has started is ignored, so it never covers "Typing…" (chat/useConversation.ts). Gate B replays it at the oracle's label time (chat/turn.ts replayScript): label:status#1 passes on all 4 turns, 63/63; the same event sent 300 ms late fails it on all 4. scripts/behaviour.mjs: a status shows as text, not markup (control: none before it); a status after text is ignored. Missing: live, Barkpark's label arrives 6-12 s after a send on the owner's Mac (the oracle's ~2.4 s), usually after the text has begun, so live turns mostly show no summary.
